checks.why: an arrow that is the value of an object-literal key is named for the key and owned by the variable the literal initialises: `impact Articles.all` answered `not declared here` because the arrow was `<arrow>` (#1585)
a function expression under a key is named the same way
a literal nested under a key is owned by the key chain
obj.x = function is named x and owned by obj
a literal under `as const` is still owned by the variable it initialises
CONTROL: a named function expression keeps its own name, not the property's
